correctness.rationale: Integral Wronskian normalization from a ten-section local-parameter leading determinant gives exact scalar c=2^30*3^14*5^6*7^3. The invariant identity B^2=A^3-1728U^7 was independently checked by integer polynomial reduction. Because p>=13, all needed factorials, scalar and group order are units, so the classical factorization reduces and agrees with the ramification divisor. The tame 168-fold quotient has special fibers of lengths 24,56,84 with ramification indices 7,3,2. Residual fiber collision occurs exactly when p divides 21962 or 27146, giving the stated divisors. Explicit finite-field jet tests at 79,139,277 corroborate, but do not replace the argument.

value.rationale: The canonical 3K-ramification divisor of a classical maximally symmetric genus-three curve has intrinsic degree 300. The result classifies every tame prime characteristic, with a sharp arithmetic transition in support cardinalities 276,164,108 and exact orbit weights. These exceptional reductions are mathematically motivated by the quotient branch locus rather than arbitrary finite cases, and the necessary integral scalar calculation identifies true exceptional primes rather than artifacts of denominator clearing.
